title: Horse Riding: Start Slow and Have Fun!
summary: Horse riding means sitting on a horse and moving with it. A good rider learns slowly, wears safe clothes, and is kind to the horse.

cover.alt: A child in a green jacket and riding helmet sits on a chestnut horse with a white blaze while a teacher in a blue cap walks beside the horse in a sandy arena.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Horse riding means sitting on a horse and moving with it. A good rider learns slowly, wears safe clothes, and is kind to the horse.

items.prompt: Have you ever seen a horse?
Do you think a horse walks fast or slowly?

blocks.title: Part 1: What Is Horse Riding?
paragraphs: People ride horses for fun, work, and sport. Some people enjoy a quiet ride outside. Police officers may ride horses at work. In the Olympic Games, riders do sports such as jumping and dressage. In dressage, the horse does careful moves when the rider asks. Horse riding is teamwork: the rider gives small signs, and the horse answers.

images.alt: A rider in an orange jacket and black helmet sits on a grey horse walking a dirt countryside path beside a meadow at sunset.

blocks.title: Check: Part 1: What Is Horse Riding?

items.answer: People ride horses for fun, work, and sport.

blocks.title: Part 2: Your First Ride
paragraphs: Horse riding for kids starts slowly at a riding school. Charlotte Dujardin also began with a quiet walk, not a race. A new rider should start at a good riding school with a teacher. The first horse is often quiet and kind. The teacher may lead the horse around an arena, which is a safe place for riding. The horse usually walks slowly. Sometimes the rider tries a short trot, which feels more bouncy. There is no need to hurry.

items.prompt: What does a new rider usually do first?
items.answer: A new rider usually rides a quiet horse at a slow walk with a teacher.
items.explanation: What would help you feel calm on your first ride, and why?

blocks.title: Part 3: Safe Clothes and Safe Moves
paragraphs: Always wear a riding helmet that fits well and is closed under your chin. A riding helmet helps protect your head if you fall. Wear strong boots that cover your ankles. Do not walk behind a horse because it may kick. Walk to the horse from the side. Talk softly and move gently, so the horse knows you are there.

images.alt: A girl in a riding helmet, green jacket, and tall black boots walks toward a chestnut horse standing beside a wooden stable, approaching from the side.

blocks.title: Check: Part 3: Safe Clothes and Safe Moves

items.prompt: How should you go near a horse?
items.answer: You should go near a horse from the side, speak softly, and move gently.

blocks.title: Part 4: The Saddle
paragraphs: A saddle is the seat on the horse’s back. A strap under the horse holds it in place. The saddle spreads the rider’s weight across the horse’s back. This helps the horse stay comfortable. Stirrups hang on both sides of the saddle. The rider puts a foot in each stirrup for balance. Boots with heels help stop the feet from sliding through.

items.prompt: What do the saddle and stirrups do?
items.answer: The saddle gives the rider a seat, and the stirrups support the rider’s feet and balance.

blocks.title: Part 5: The Reins
paragraphs: Reins are long straps that go from the rider’s hands to the horse’s bridle. The bridle is the gear on the horse’s head. Reins help a rider ask the horse to turn, slow down, or stop. They are a little like a steering wheel, but riders must use small, soft moves. Pulling hard can hurt the horse. Riders also use their legs and body.

items.prompt: Why should a rider use the reins softly?
items.answer: A rider should use the reins softly because hard pulling can hurt the horse.

blocks.title: Part 6: Famous Riders
paragraphs: Charlotte Dujardin rode Valegro in dressage. They won individual Olympic gold in London in 2012 and Rio in 2016. Frankie Dettori was a famous race rider. In 1996, he won all seven races on one day at Ascot. Ron Turcotte rode the fast racehorse Secretariat, which won the US Triple Crown in 1973. Famous riders go fast or do hard moves, but new riders begin with a slow walk.

images.alt: A dressage rider in a dark coat, white breeches, and helmet sits on a black horse with a braided mane walking in a sandy arena before empty wooden stands.

items.prompt: How is a new rider different from these famous riders?
items.answer: A new rider starts with a slow walk, but famous riders race or do difficult moves.
